decisions.quote:
Some have reported

     evidence for the decoy effect in perceptual tasks (Choplin & Hummel, 2005; Parrish, Evans, &

     Beran, 2015; Trueblood, Brown, Heathcote, & Busemeyer, 2013), whereas others have not

     (Parrish, Dawes, & Thompson, 2024; Spektor, Kellen, & Hotaling, 2018; Spektor, Bhatia, &

     Gluth, 2021). A strikingly clean design was offered by Parrish et al. (2015), who demonstrated

     the decoy effect in a perceptual discrimination task with rhesus macaques. In the present study,

     we sought to extend their paradigm to human participants to determine whether the same effect

     would emerge.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not yet exist. The paper re-tests only one original study: Parrish, Evans, and Beran (2015), "Rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) exhibit the decoy effect in a perceptual discrimination task" (Attention, Perception & Psychophysics, 77(5), 1715-1725, DOI 10.3758/s13414-015-0885-6, Experiment 2), which is already represented by shipped row 377 (paired to blind target_index 0). Shipped row 554 refers to the 2014 conference abstract by Parrish and Beran (DOI 10.1037/e524912015-308, "Rhesus Monkeys Fall for the Decoy Effect in a Perceptual Discrimination Task"), which is never cited or mentioned in the paper and is excluded by the codebook rule against coding a meeting abstract alongside or instead of the published article. Row 554 is therefore a redundant alternate-report row and must be removed. Parent independently confirms the published-article binding and redundant meeting-report removal. The schema requires the target_index member to be absent for a row removal; the old null member caused the scientifically justified removal to remain unapplied. This is a new independently source-validated canonical decision, not a repair of the immutable provider reply.

decisions.quote:
Using the rhesus-macaque paradigm from Parrish et al. (2015), we

     tested whether a perceptual decoy effect generalizes to humans. Participants (n = 50) completed

     400 trials. Contrary to our preregistered prediction, we found no reliable decoy effect.
decisions.reason: This original row is source-confirmed for removal: its alternate meeting report or unrelated original is not an independently retested empirical target in this paper. The valid published target and its outcome remain on retained row 377. The paper type is replication, independently corrected as such; paper type is not a reason to transfer a retained target outcome onto an invalid original. Outcome for this removed pair is conditionally inapplicable, not an evidence-access ambiguity or failed execution. The earlier categorical cannot_be_determined and mistaken type dependency remain preserved in immutable raw history.
